clue.text: Boring group, but absolutely determined

parts.note: something boring is dead, lifeless and dull
a set is a group of things that belong together

explanation.surface: A dull bunch of people who are nonetheless utterly resolute.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dead set on something is an idiom for being fixed in one's resolve.

clue.text: Clean bed to doctor's advantage

parts.note: Dr is the title abbreviation for doctor; the 's just links it to what follows
having the edge means having an advantage

explanation.surface: Making the bed works out well for the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a river or sea bed, not a bed to sleep in.
explanation.definitionFit: To dredge is to scoop silt and mud from a riverbed or harbour floor to clear it.

clue.text: Uncivilised person turns plate upside down

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is turned so it reads from the bottom up
upside down completes the instruction to read the word bottom to top

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer

explanation.surface: A brute flips a dinner plate over.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone an animal is to call them a brutish, savage person.

clue.text: Crinkly fabric conceals visionary with soft touch

parts.note: a seer is a prophet who sees visions
a soft touch is someone easily fooled, a sucker

explanation.surface: A puckered cloth hides a prophet who has a gentle hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Seersucker is a lightweight cotton cloth with a puckered, striped texture.

clue.text: This is thanks to unfinished book being banned

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: the word book taken as written, before its end is cut

explanation.surface: Thanks to an incomplete volume, it has been forbidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is prohibited by social custom, forbidden.

clue.text: Curled up tabby is to look after a little one

indicators.note: a cat curled up is twisted into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cat curled up asleep is a kind of nursemaid for a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: To babysit is to mind someone's young child while the parents are out.

clue.text: Lewd, dissolute kiss interrupted by end of feature film, starring Bing Crosby

parts.note: blue means smutty or indecent

indicators.note: a letter breaks into the rearranged word
dissolute means loose, so the letters of kiss come apart and are rearranged

parts.note: the word kiss taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: end of means take the last letter of feature

parts.note: the word feature supplies only its final letter

explanation.surface: An indecent kiss is cut into a feature film with the crooner.
explanation.walkthrough: Feature looks like part of the definition, feature film, but it only gives its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue Skies is a 1946 Irving Berlin musical in which Crosby starred alongside Fred Astaire.

clue.text: Flying mammal gets hot in tub

parts.note: the bat is the only mammal capable of true flight

explanation.surface: A bat ends up warm in a bathtub.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath is a large tub for washing the body.

clue.text: Fondness for pulpy jam

parts.note: pulpy means soft and squashy
a jam is a tight spot, a predicament

explanation.surface: A liking for mushy preserves.
explanation.walkthrough: Jam reads as the fruit spread but means a difficult situation.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a soft spot for something is an idiom for an affectionate liking.

clue.text: Informer had to identify dog, we hear

parts.note: to tell one thing from another is to identify it

indicators.note: we hear means the pieces are taken by their sound, not spelling

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them, to tail them

explanation.surface: A snitch had to point out which dog it was.
explanation.walkthrough: Dog is a verb here, meaning to follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale is someone who reports others' wrongdoing, a sneak.

clue.text: Cast out one-time partner and lie around

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or lover

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of lie are turned about and jumbled

parts.note: the word lie taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Throw out your former partner and tell lies about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to banish or expel them from their homeland.

clue.text: Overflowing but foul in shape

indicators.note: in shape here means put into a new form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters of these three clue words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something brimming over yet in a nasty condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bountiful harvest is plentiful, abundant to the point of excess.

clue.text: German girl meets family in prison

parts.note: lass is a northern British and Scottish word for a girl
a house is a family line, as in the House of Windsor

explanation.surface: A young German woman joins her relatives behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: In British army slang the glasshouse is a military prison, from the glass roof of the one at Aldershot.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasshouse is British military slang for a jail where soldiers serve detention.

clue.text: Is not still the same when love has gone

indicators.note: when the love has gone, that letter is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: points back to the clue's opening words, which are used again as the letters to work on
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A wistful line: nothing remains the same once love is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition doubles as the fodder: take the O out of the two words and the contraction still means the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The contraction is the everyday shortened form of the two words, with identical meaning.

clue.text: Dad, we converted a number which is hard to carry

indicators.note: converted means changed into a different form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word Dad taken as written, part of the material rearranged
the word we taken as written, part of the material rearranged
eight is simply a number

explanation.surface: Dad and I changed a figure that proved burdensome.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead weight is a heavy, inert load that is awkward to lift.

clue.text: Mock one who exists on balm and medicine

parts.note: cod as an adjective means sham or mock, as in cod Latin
a liver is literally someone who lives
a soothing balm is often an oil

explanation.surface: Teasing a person who survives on ointment and pills.
explanation.definitionFit: This fishy oil is a traditional dietary supplement spooned to children as a health remedy.

clue.text: Weary Willie having an affair with Fanny Adams?

definitions.note: Weary Willie is old British slang for a shirker or idler

parts.note: do is slang for having sex with someone
sweet Fanny Adams is British slang for nothing at all

explanation.surface: A tired chap called Willie is carrying on with a woman named Fanny.
explanation.walkthrough: Fanny Adams looks like a lover's name but is British slang, from sweet FA, meaning nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A do-nothing is an idle, lazy person, just like the shiftless loafer the old nickname describes.

clue.text: Penniless deputy needing shares to rise

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: parts are portions or shares

explanation.surface: A broke deputy needs his stocks to go up.
explanation.walkthrough: Shares suggests the stock market but just means portions.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapped, as in strapped for cash, is an informal word for short of money.

clue.text: Produced by lectures, naturally

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: belonging to a course of lectures
second meaning: certainly, as you would expect

explanation.walkthrough: A series of lectures forms a course, so what comes from them is literally part of a course.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an everyday way of saying obviously or certainly, while literally meaning belonging to a course.

clue.text: Puffed up, having smelled sweet to start with

indicators.note: the sweet is placed at the start, before the other piece

parts.note: toffee is a chewy sweet, a candy
nosed means sniffed or smelled out

explanation.surface: Someone inflated after catching the scent of candy.
explanation.walkthrough: Toffee-nosed is British slang for snobbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Puffed up here means conceited and snooty, which is what the British slang term describes.

clue.text: Kind of dance for a stick-in-the-mud?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... dance, a folk dance for four couples
second meaning: a dull, conventional person

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are a country dance and an old-fashioned person.
explanation.definitionFit: A square is slang for a conventional, unfashionable person, and square dancing is a folk dance form.

clue.text: Guard makes second appearance

parts.note: an actor's entry is their appearance on stage

explanation.surface: A sentinel comes onto the scene a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted to keep watch, a guard.

clue.text: Crazy mother turns on the green light

indicators.note: the mother word turns round and is read backwards

parts.note: giving the OK is giving the green light, permission

explanation.surface: An unhinged mum switches on a green lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Running amok is behaving wildly and uncontrollably, out of one's mind.

clue.text: Imposing bust half-squeezed

parts.note: a bust is a sculpture, a kind of statue
half of the word squeezed: its first four of eight letters

explanation.surface: An impressive bosom squeezed in at the half.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuesque describes a tall, dignified, impressive figure, like a sculpture.

clue.text: Water with gas in it, too nice not to be finished

parts.note: the word too taken as written, losing its last letter

indicators.note: neither word is allowed to finish: each loses its final letter

parts.note: the word nice taken as written, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Fizzy water is just too pleasant to leave undrunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The instruction applies to both words, too and nice, each losing its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic water is a carbonated mixer flavoured with quinine.

clue.text: Skirt: Mum needed to get smallest

indicators.note: the answer needs the word Mum added to make smallest, so take it away from that word

parts.note: the minimum is the smallest amount possible
the word Mum taken as written, the part to subtract

explanation.surface: A short skirt, with Mum needed to make it the tiniest.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as the answer plus Mum making smallest; subtract Mum to find it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mini is a very short skirt, the miniskirt of the 1960s.

clue.text: Move to pride in place for sinners

indicators.note: move tells us to shift these letters around into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these three clue words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Relocate pride to where wrongdoers end up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole of 'place for sinners'; pride, a deadly sin, adds to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdition is eternal damnation, the hellish fate awaiting the wicked.

clue.text: John of Scotland in a sports car is a great person

indicators.note: one name sits inside the car abbreviation

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, labels a fast touring sports car
Ian is the Scottish form of the name John

explanation.surface: A Scotsman called John in a racy car is a big shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A giant is figuratively someone of towering ability or importance.

clue.text: Fancy Meg and Enid conceiving!

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamented, so the names are rearranged

parts.note: the name Meg taken as written, part of the material rearranged
the name Enid taken as written, part of the material rearranged

explanation.surface: Imagine two women, Meg and Enid, both pregnant!
explanation.walkthrough: Conceiving looks like pregnancy but means forming an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Deeming is considering or judging, as conceiving an idea or view is.

clue.text: Where to find Felix & Co hostile without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: catty means spiteful or hostile
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A cartoon cat's gang are hostile, never pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: Without looks like it means removing the hesitation, but it means outside it. Felix is a famous cartoon cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattery is a boarding establishment where cats are kept.
